title_en: Interpretation of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Nationality Law of the People's Republic of China in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region

articles.content_en: 1. All Hong Kong residents who are of Chinese descent and born in the Chinese territory (including Hong Kong), as well as those who meet the conditions for having Chinese nationality as prescribed in the Nationality Law of the People's Republic of China, shall be Chinese citizens.

2. All Chinese compatriots in Hong Kong, regardless of whether they hold a “British Dependent Territories Citizens Passport” or a “British National (Overseas) Passport”, shall be Chinese citizens. As from July 1, 1997, the aforementioned Chinese citizens may continue to use valid travel documents issued by the British Government for travel to other countries or regions; however, they shall not be entitled to British consular protection in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region and other parts of the People's Republic of China by virtue of holding the above-mentioned British travel documents.

3. Any Chinese citizen in Hong Kong who has acquired British citizenship under the British Government's “Right of Abode in the United Kingdom Scheme” shall not be recognized as such according to the Nationality Law of the People's Republic of China. Such persons shall remain Chinese citizens and shall not be entitled to British consular protection in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region and other parts of the People's Republic of China.

4. Chinese citizens of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region who have the right of abode in foreign countries may use relevant documents issued by foreign governments for travel to other countries or regions; however, they shall not be entitled to foreign consular protection in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region and other parts of the People's Republic of China by virtue of holding the above-mentioned documents.

5. Where there is any change in the nationality of a Chinese citizen of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, he or she may declare such change to the competent authority of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region for handling nationality applications by presenting valid documents.

6. The Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region is authorized to designate the Immigration Department of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region as the authority for handling nationality applications in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region. The Immigration Department of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region shall process all matters relating to nationality applications in accordance with the Nationality Law of the People's Republic of China and the provisions above.
